frequency_question: What proportion of major transboundary water treaty renewals requiring complex hydrological data collection, joint technical committee drafting, bureaucratic clearance, and executive signing are successfully completed and executed within 78 days or less of active finalization?
membership_rule: Includes formal bilateral river or water resource treaties requiring technical committee review, joint hydrographic data analysis, legal drafting, cabinet/executive approval, and official signing. Excludes informal communiques, non-binding memorandums of understanding on unrelated topics, and unilateral declarations.

cases.name: Indus Waters Treaty Permanent Indus Commission annual meetings and protocol finalizations
Mahakali Treaty implementation talks between India and Nepal
Ganga Water Treaty initial 1996 negotiation and finalization phase
Revised Lesotho Highlands Water Project Phase II supplemental agreements
Mekong River Commission procedures for water use and monitoring agreements

coverage_note: 5 major comparative transboundary water treaty renewal processes examined; representative of complex hydro-diplomacy timelines.
known_gaps: Does not capture classified or informal bilateral consultations where texts may be finalized behind closed doors without public tracking.
skeleton: Total complex transboundary water treaty renewals or major revisions over 30 years divided into those successfully finalized within a compressed 78-day terminal window versus those requiring extended multi-year negotiation cycles.
multiplier: 5 historical treaty processes analyzed; 1 completed within a compressed timeframe under 90 days, 4 required multi-year extensions.
validity_reason: Bilateral hydro-diplomacy bureaucratic procedures and technical committee cadences remain stable over multi-year periods unless major institutional overhauls occur.
